_source: Balluff BIC007H (BIC 2B0-IT1A7-Q40KFU-SM4A5A) inductive coupler, recorded product page (426 kB). Verified in the page: `IP67` ×3, `PBTP` ×3 (housing material), `40 x 40 x 62` ×3 (dimensions), `1.7 A` ×3.
_tier: value-verified. Highest-yield fixture left unpromoted (177 attributes), chosen on the theory that a high yield is where GARBAGE hides. It was: an Alpine.js/Tailwind front-end framework was leaking its conditional class bindings into the attribute list.

_notes.alpine_bindings: This fixture found P1.4c. Alpine.js writes conditional classes as an object literal — `:class="{ 'shadow-md': !searchOpen && !mobileMenuOpen, 'w-0': menuOpenedId !== '0' }"` — and splitting that on `:` produced attributes like `'shadow-md'` = `!searchOpen && !mobileMenuOpen`. The existing code-fragment rule missed them because they name no DOM global and call no method; `&&`, `||`, `!==`, `===` and a leading `!identifier` cannot occur in a specification value.
_notes.torn_quotes: A second, subtler form: the split also lands on a colon INSIDE the class name, because that is Tailwind's responsive prefix. `'absolute inset-x-0 px-2 mx-2 lg:mx-0 …': searchOpen` became the label `'absolute inset-x-0 px-2 mx-2 lg` — an opening quote with no closing one. Rejected by shape, requiring the quote to be at the START and an object-literal `':` for the value form, so a real apostrophe ("Manufacturer's data") survives.
_notes.measured: 177 → 161 attributes with all 8 normalized fields unchanged, so the removed 16 were pure framework noise.
_notes.temperature: -5 / 55 °C comes from the min/max row pairing added in P1.4a — Balluff uses the same two-row layout as Turck, which is why that fix pays off across vendors rather than for one page.
